title.en: Economics: Industrial Clusters in Tamil Nadu

text.en: Raju saw rows of power looms in Erode. "Why are the same industries in the same place?" he asked.

An industrial cluster is a group of firms of the same industry in one area that share skills, suppliers and markets. Tamil Nadu has many famous clusters.
Examples are Tiruppur for knitwear, Coimbatore for textiles and pumps, Sivakasi for fireworks and printing, Karur for home textiles, Salem for steel and Erode for textiles, and Ambattur and Hosur for engineering.
Clusters create jobs, make goods cheaper and spread skills, but they need good roads, power, water and care for the environment. Small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) form the backbone of the clusters.

Think about why textile units cluster in Tiruppur or cracker factories cluster in Sivakasi instead of scattering across distant districts.

board.text: Why industries group in one place

text.en: Economist Alfred Marshall called these industrial districts. Firms nearby share trained workers, specialised suppliers, repair workshops and transport hubs.
When many similar firms locate together, external economies lower costs for every firm, even tiny workshops.
Historically, handloom weaving, metalwork and tanning grew from local craft skills. Later, colonial rail links, electricity and rural entrepreneurship helped modern factories grow.

board.text: From traditional crafts to modern clusters

text.en: In the Coimbatore region, groundwater irrigation and cotton cultivation led first to spinning mills, and then to textile machinery and electric motor pumps.
Coimbatore now supplies nearly half of India's agricultural water pumps and is famously known as the Manchester of South India.

board.text: Coimbatore: pumps & Manchester of South India

text.en: Just nearby, Tiruppur grew from cotton ginning into a global knitwear export hub, stitching T-shirts and hosiery for major world brands.
Erode and Salem form strong weaving and powerloom belts, while Salem also hosts steel, sago and mineral-based industries.
Karur specialises in woven home textiles like bedsheets, table linen and curtains, alongside bus body building for vehicles across India.

board.text: Karur: home textiles & bus body building

text.en: Further south, Sivakasi is known across India as 'Kutty Japan' for printing, notebooks, matchboxes and fireworks.
Around Chennai—in Ambattur, Guindy, Sriperumbudur and Oragadam—a massive automobile and electronics corridor has developed near deep-water ports.
In Krishnagiri district, Hosur emerged as an industrial city near Bengaluru, building two-wheelers, trucks, precision tools and EVs.
Along the Palar river valley—Vellore, Ranipet, Ambur and Vaniyambadi—lies India's leading leather tanning and footwear export cluster.

board.text: Palar valley: Ambur & Ranipet leather cluster

text.en: Across Tamil Nadu, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises—or MSMEs—handle dyeing, stitching, casting, packaging and component supply for big factories.
Two forces keep clusters competitive: horizontal division of labour across steps like spinning, dyeing and stitching, and vertical ties with buyers and toolmakers.
Tamil Nadu's state agencies actively nurture these clusters through industrial estates, TIDCO joint ventures and SIPCOT industrial parks.
SIDCO builds small plots and sheds for MSMEs, while SIPCOT develops large estates with roads, water and effluent treatment facilities.

board.text: SIDCO for MSMEs; SIPCOT for large estates

text.en: Today Tamil Nadu ranks among India's top three industrialised states, with balanced manufacturing spread across multiple Tier-2 cities rather than just one metro.
Success also brings serious challenges: textile dyeing and leather tanning use large amounts of water and can pollute rivers like the Noyyal and Palar.
In response, courts and industry associations built Common Effluent Treatment Plants and Zero Liquid Discharge systems to recycle factory wastewater.
Another modern challenge is rising automation and competition from Bangladesh and Vietnam in low-cost garments, pushing TN clusters toward higher quality.
At the policy level, strong technical colleges, polytechnics and ITIs feed skilled engineers and technicians directly into nearby clusters every year.
To recap the map of TN clusters: Tiruppur for knitwear, Karur for home textiles, Coimbatore for pumps, Hosur for autos, Ambur for leather and Sivakasi for printing.

board.text: Recap: key TN clusters by specialty

text.en: To trace the big causal chain: local resources & enterprise -> shared skilled labour -> lower costs & MSME ecosystem -> export competitiveness.
Balancing rapid industrial job growth with clean rivers and worker safety is the key to sustainable industrial clusters in Tamil Nadu.

board.text: Sustainable growth with clean water & safety
